In der Volkskamera einfügen: Einstellung: To add it in Volkskamera: Settings → ★ Combinations → Paste.
Die Volkskamera filmt wie eine analoge F: Volkskamera films like an analogue movie camera. You choose a real film stock – from the cinema film of the 1890s to today’s slide film – and the app gives the picture its colours, contrast and grain. As with a real camera, every film has a fixed sensitivity; you control brightness with the shutter speed.
Der große Knopf startet und beendet die: The large button starts and stops recording; while recording, the pause button appears next to it. Tap the viewfinder to focus there. After filming, the film is developed (progress shown in the thumbnail at the bottom right) and saved to your gallery in the folder “Movies/VolksKamera”.
FPS: frame rate of the finished film (e.g. 18 for silent-film judder, 24 for cinema).
FORMAT: aspect ratio 4:3 or 16:9.
LENS: switches between the phone’s cameras (wide, normal, tele).
SHUTTER: shutter speed from 1/5 to 1/5000 second. Shorter times make the picture darker and movement sharper. There is deliberately no automatic mode: brightness follows only shutter speed and film – even when focusing or changing lenses.
ISO / ASA: shows the fixed sensitivity of the chosen film. The app exposes the sensor exactly as the real film would have been exposed at this shutter speed – so an ISO 8 film needs a lot of light or long exposures.
Tap a counter to advance it.
Unter „Aufnahme“ wählst du die Auflösung: Under “Recording” you choose the resolution of the finished film (480p, 576p, 720p, 1080p) and whether the front camera records mirrored (also directly in the camera with the ⇋ button). With “Calibrate sensor” the app measures once how your phone processes its camera image and compensates for it before every film – the instructions there show what a good calibration scene looks like.
Unter „★ Kombinationen“ speicherst du Fi: Under “★ Combinations” you save film, colour filter and sound (microphone, noise, crackle, hum) under a name. With “Share” you send it to others as a short text; anyone who shares or pastes it into Volkskamera can use it.
Zahnrad → Hersteller → Breite (8, 16 ode: Gear → manufacturer → gauge (8, 16 or 35 mm) → film. Tapping a film shows its profile: sample image, characteristics and description. The ◐ button next to the sample image compares it with the original. The film is only applied when you tap “Use”.
Oben in der Filmauswahl wählst du, woran: At the top of the film selection you choose the picture the films are shown on: Terrace, Fröruper Berge or a photo from your own gallery – ideally one with sky, green, red and skin tones.
Bei S/W-Filmen kannst du wie früher eine: With black-and-white films you can put a colour filter in front of the lens, just like in the old days. It lightens its own colour and darkens the complementary colour: yellow for natural clouds, orange and red for dramatic skies, green for bright foliage. Each filter lists its Kodak Wratten number, the B+W and Hoya names and what it is used for. The filter applies to all black-and-white films until you remove it.
Filme bearbeiten und eigene LUTs: Editing films and your own LUTs
„Bearbeiten“ öffnet den LUT-Editor: Beli: “Edit” opens the LUT editor: exposure, contrast, black and white point, colour temperature, saturation, colour channels and split toning. Press and hold to see the film original. You save your version as your own LUT – the film’s original LUT is always kept. You find your LUTs in the film selection under “★ My LUTs”.
Unter „Mikrofon“ wählst du die Aufnahmek: Under “Microphone” you choose the recording chain of an era – from the Edison phonograph via carbon, ribbon and valve microphones to the camcorder – sorted by decade or type, each with a profile. Controls: noise (0 = silent), noise gate against the hiss of the phone microphone, distortion, bandwidth, automatic gain. “Original sound” leaves the sound unchanged.
Knacken wie von einer alten Filmkopie. B: Crackle like an old film print. Hum like a cable problem: ground loop, loose contact, mobile-phone interference (the “dit-dit-dit”), dimmer or buzz – at 50 Hz (Europe) or 60 Hz (USA).
Nimm eine kurze Sprachprobe auf (3, 5 od: Record a short voice sample (3, 5 or 8 seconds) and hear it as it will sound in the finished film. The sample is played once and not saved.
Unter „Gehäuse“ gestaltest du deine Kame: Under “Body” you design your camera: material (leather, fabric, wood, metal, stone or your own photo), the metal of the fittings, the shutter button and the lettering – text, font and metal are freely selectable.
Die Materialien werden mit Licht gerechn: The materials are rendered with light: relief, gloss and reflections. With “Light follows movement” the lamp stays fixed in the room – when you tilt or turn the phone, highlights and shadows move as on a real camera. Strength and colour of the light are adjustable. With a front-camera photo your room is reflected in the body. If it bothers you, simply switch it off; the light then comes from the top left.
Unter „Gehäuse“ → „App-Symbol“ wählst du: Under “Body” → “App icon” you choose one of four Art Deco icons. The home screen picks it up after a few seconds; with some launchers the app has to be placed on the home screen again afterwards.
Das Vorschaubild unten rechts öffnet den: The thumbnail at the bottom right opens the most recently developed film. From there you get to the overview of all films and to the editor, where you join several films with fades, countdown or film burn.
Eine Kombination merkt sich Film, Farbfi: A combination remembers film, colour filter and sound (microphone, noise, crackle, hum) – to switch quickly or to share with others.
In der Zwischenablage ist keine Volkskam: The clipboard does not contain a Volkskamera combination.
Auflösung des fertigen Films (kurze Seit: Resolution of the finished film (short side). 480p and 576p correspond to old video and TV standards, 1080p is full HD.
Umschalten geht auch direkt in der Kamer: You can also switch directly in the camera with the ⇋ button when the front camera is active.
Jedes Handy bearbeitet sein Kamerabild a: Every phone processes its camera image differently – with more saturation and more contrast than the sensor really sees. Volkskamera’s films are calculated for a neutral image. With calibration the app measures once how your phone changes the image and compensates for it before every film.
1. Lege Gegenstände mit vielen kräftige:
1.  Put together objects with lots of strong colours – for example coloured pencils or felt pens – plus something white and something dark.
2.  Make sure the light is even: daylight from a window is ideal, no direct backlight, no hard shadows.
3.  Hold the phone steady so that the colours fill most of the picture.
4.  Tap “Calibrate now”. The app takes a raw image and a normal image at the same time and compares them.

Beispiel einer guten Kalibrier-Szene: vi: Example of a good calibration scene: many colours, one light and one dark area, even light. Left the phone’s image, right the same shot developed neutrally – calibration compensates exactly for this difference.

Rauschen = Eigenrauschen des alten Gerät: Noise = self-noise of the old device (0 = completely silent). The noise gate reduces the hiss of the phone microphone in quiet passages.
Die Probe klingt wie der fertige Film un: The sample sounds like the finished film and is played once. It is not saved.
Unten Filme antippen, um sie hinzuzufüge: Tap films below to add them.
